This decade is key for major automakers and OEMs looking to commercialise solid-state batteries in electric vehicle applications.

Over the past year, several incumbent battery cell producers and automakers have committed to a demonstration of solid-state electric vehicles by 2027 with large-scale production by 2030.

Both of the world’s largest battery makers, CATL and BYD are committed to producing demonstration solid-state vehicles this decade, whilst BYD recently said it was targeting 2030 for mass production.

“Solid-state technologies are in the middle of a four to six year qualification cycle, so these timelines match up well with forecast commercial delivery timelines,” said Rory McNulty, Benchmark’s Product Director for New Technology.

#### Which companies are committing to solid-state technology this decade?

Although the technologies being qualified today won’t be seen in commercial cars for at least a few years, the end of 2024 saw several Chinese players roll out vehicles with semi-solid-state batteries using traditional anode materials.

“With more expected in 2025, this may have been a catalyst for some of the recent timeline announcements we are seeing,” McNulty said.

!This decade is key for solid-state EV commercialisation

Although automotive timelines represent the industry’s ambition to make the most of the performance gains of solid-state batteries this decade, it is the cell makers who will ultimately enable this.

Samsung, LG Energy Solution, CATL, EVE Energy, and Sunwoda are amongst the largest cell makers that have committed to 2027 to produce solid-state batteries at least at the demonstration scale.

#### What solid-state technologies are these companies using?

The solid-state batteries currently deployed in vehicular applications use semi-solid-state technologies in which a small quantity of liquid electrolyte is added to improve the contact of the anode and cathode to the solid electrolyte.

They also use more traditional anode materials such as graphite or graphite-silicon composites, meaning the energy density gains aren’t as large as they could be.

“The key differentiator for technologies undergoing qualification today, is that they are looking to employ next-generation anode materials, which could provide a really significant leap in energy density,” McNulty said.

_To learn more about trends in emerging battery technologies, download Benchmark’s free special issue,_ _Cheaper, Better, and Smaller: The Future of Battery Technology_ _._

**Upstream and downstream policy push: Europe Regional Spotlight** \\

Compared with China and the US, Europe’s upstream and downstream footprint in the global battery supply chain footprint is small. No major critical mineral used in the sector is mined or processed primarily on the continent, nor are cathode, anode or cell development and installation centred on the continent. However, a package of policies under the EU’s Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) is looking to boost its manufacturing presence in the industry, required if Europe is to meet more of its own demand for electric vehicles (EVs) and battery energy stationary storage (BESS), both of which are anticipated to grow significantly through to 2040.](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/upstream-and-downstream-policy-push-europe-regional-spotlight)

Oct 09, 2026\\
\\
**Lithium cost pass-through drives volatile quarter for energy storage cells: Cell Price Review Q3 2026** \\
\\
Battery cell prices fell across nearly every grade in Q3 2026, but the path differed sharply by format.\\
\\
For instance, Benchmark’s LFP Prismatic 314Ah EXW China and CIF Europe prices ended the quarter lower after a pronounced July spike, Benchmark’s LFP Prismatic 314Ah CIF North America prices were broadly unchanged, and the Benchmark Lithium Ion Battery Global price closed the quarter at its lowest level of the period.\\
\\
"Overall, Q3 was defined by the delayed transmission of lithium volatility into cell pricing, most visibly in ESS formats, alongside a regional divergence that left North American prices at a premium to Europe by quarter-end as freight costs rose," said Adam Megginson, a principal price analyst at Benchmark.](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/lithium-cost-pass-through-drives-volatile-quarter-for-energy-storage-cells-cell-price-review-q3-2026)

**UK considering alignment with EU over tariff on Chinese EVs** \\
\\
While countries including the US, Turkey, and Mexico have been ramping up tariffs on electric vehicles (EVs) made in China, EV imports from China into the UK have continued to face a standard 10% import duty. The UK’s largest trading partner, the EU, introduced tariffs on China-made BEVs in 2024.\\
\\
In 2023, the last year when EVs made in China did not face additional tariffs from the EU, they accounted for 17% of total EV sales within the bloc. They broadly maintained this share until 2026, when over the first eight months of the year that share increased to 22% as Chinese automakers push into overseas markets against the backdrop of their subdued domestic environment. In comparison, China-made EVs accounted for 19% of EV sales in the UK in 2023, with that figure rising to 33% so far in 2026.](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/uk-considering-alignment-with-eu-over-tariff-on-chinese-evs)

\\
Oct 06, 2026\\
\\
**Can Cobre Panama copper mine run for 25 years without growing?** \\
\\
A commission convened by Panama’s government to decide how to manage the country’s controversial Cobre Panama copper mine has recommended 25 years of operation but without expanding the site’s physical footprint. The mine, run by First Quantum Minerals, was closed in 2023 after it was ruled unconstitutional following protests against its operation.\\
\\
The report also recommends steadily shrinking the existing footprint over this time, before eight years of “active closure” and 30 years of post-closure monitoring. Other non-negotiable criteria for reopening the site include compliance with existing Supreme Court rulings and laws around the project, ownership by the state, and the project must be financially self-sustaining. The report also calls for data transparency and supervision of the site to international standards, and priority given to concerns among affected Panamanian communities and businesses.](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/can-cobre-panama-copper-mine-run-for-25-years-without-growing-)

**How can African nations benefit from the region’s battery mineral resources?** \\
\\
In recent years, Africa has rapidly grown from a small player in the global battery supply chain to a strategically significant one, as global players begin to realise the potential of the region’s resources.\\
\\
As Europe and North America in particular look to diversify their China-centric supply chains, African nations are emerging as key trade partners.\\
\\
Africa’s growing role in the global battery supply chain and how countries in the region can best capture value from this were key points of discussion at Benchmark’s Giga Africa event in Marrakesh, Morocco.](https://source.benchmarkminerals.com/article/how-can-african-nations-benefit-from-the-region-s-battery-mineral-resources-)
